title: Minimum Cost Server Coverage
statement:
You manage a row of `n` servers numbered `1` to `n` from left to right. Server `i` has a positive cost `cost[i]`.

When you select server `i`, you pay `cost[i]` and server `i` itself plus the next `i` servers, that is servers `i + 1` through `min(2i, n)`, are covered automatically. A server is covered if it is selected or lies inside the range covered by some selected server.

You are allowed to select a server that is already covered. Sometimes this is worthwhile: a cheap server further along may extend the covered range much further than the servers before it. Note that server `1` is never covered by anything else, so it must always be selected.

Return the **minimum total cost** of a set of selected servers such that all `n` servers are covered.

**Follow-up:** a solution that keeps the candidates in a heap runs in `O(n log n)`. Can you bring it down to `O(n)`?
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `cost[1], cost[2], ..., cost[n]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum total cost.

examples.explanation: Server 1 must be selected (cost 3) and covers server 2. Server 3 is still uncovered. Selecting server 2 as well (cost 1, although it is already covered) covers servers 3 and 4, so everything is covered for 3 + 1 = 4. Selecting server 3 instead costs 3 + 2 = 5.
Selecting server 1 (cost 4) covers servers 1 and 2. Server 3 is not covered, but it is cheap: selecting it (cost 1) covers servers 3 through 6, which includes servers 4 and 5. Total 4 + 1 = 5.
Select server 1 (cost 1), which covers server 2. Select server 3 (cost 1), which covers servers 3 and 4. Total 2; the expensive server 2 is never needed.

hints: Let f[i] be the cheapest way to cover servers i..n if you select server i and servers 1..i-1 are already covered. What can the next selected server be?
After selecting i, servers up to 2i are covered, so the next selected server j must satisfy i < j ≤ 2i + 1. If 2i ≥ n you are done. Otherwise f[i] = cost[i] + min f[j] over that range.
The window i+1..2i+1 slides leftwards as i decreases, and both ends only move left. A monotonic deque gives each window minimum in amortised O(1).
